text: Galaxy Research: Bitcoin reclaiming $82,470 could provide stronger confirmation of a cycle bottom Galaxy Research backtested Bitcoin's historical bear markets using a rule of a 50%+ closing-price drawdown lasting at least 90 days, covering six completed cycles since 2011 and the current drawdown. The study found that 50-day moving average (50d MA) reclaims are fast but unreliable: 43 of 106 reclaims failed across past bears, and the first reclaim failed in every cycle. By contrast, the 50-week moving average (50w MA) provided a stronger signal, with only 2 failures out of 13 reclaims. BTC is currently trading around $77,500, up 32.4% from the June 30 low, with the 50w MA at $82,470. text: Rust Supply Chain Attack Hits Widely Used Crates With Solana Ecosystem Exposure Security researchers including SlowMist, Socket and StepSecurity reported a coordinated supply chain attack affecting arrayref@0.3.10, internment@0.8.7 and append-only-vec@0.1.9. The malicious releases introduced a typosquatted proc-macro1 dependency whose build script downloaded and executed a remote payload during Cargo builds, meaning simply compiling an affected dependency could compromise a developer or CI host. Rust's security team removed the malicious releases and locked the maintainer account, saying the maintainer's machine or publishing credentials were likely compromised. arrayref is widely used across the Rust ecosystem, including dependency chains involving Solana-related components, though this does not mean those downstream projects were compromised. — link

QCP desk data show aggressive perpetual buying running well ahead of spot on Wednesday while open interest remained broadly unchanged. Leverage then rebuilt as price extended on Thursday. Spot demand followed. US spot BTC ETFs recorded $517m of net inflows on Wednesday, their strongest day since May, while perpetual funding has since moderated from its local highs without a comparable retracement in BTC. Options have repriced too, with front-end implied volatility rising sharply from the subdued summer regime, even as downside skew remains relatively contained. The broader question is bigger than the size of the Treasury buybacks. Long-end yields, sovereign issuance and AI-related borrowing are increasingly competing for the same pool of capital, making duration an important part of crypto's macro backdrop. text: The bull is slowly returning. Dovish talks of rates easing, Trump bringing Hyperliquid to U.S clients and the fed lighting the candle for BTC. Bessent drew a line in the sand with the 30y, said they won't let rates above current prices or I will intervene with QE while SPX is at the highs. Correct me if I'm wrong but this is the first genuine signs from the fed regarding debasement/inflation we've seen in several months. The market is calling their bluff, 30y is sending which now forces Bessents hand to back his words. They either deploy the new liquidity support buyback operations or let yields spiral out of control. Pretty confident the writing is on the wall where BTC and Gold become the immediate movers. A thesis for BTC and majors here is that Trump is beginning to have limited impact on AI companies. They become larger and harder to push once they reach a productivity wall like they've been doing since post Fable. There's a lot of liquidity in the system, it would be far easier to turn the boosters on and multiple their wealth once again through decentralized nefarious means. Open source models are catching up and becoming significantly more popular, users are realizing they don't need Fable type capabilities 24/7. Why would you hire an elite engineer to do the work of a typical plumber? Models are becoming very capable while also effectively becoming dirt cheap. What I'm seeing as the biggest risk for tradfi/AI is this productivity wall increasing as Anthropic goes to IPO. I'm not a power user of Claude so my observations are more so from a holistic view of devs opinions. The successor to Fable is to release somewhere around late September. Anthropic will need to dig their claws into presenting this as god 2.0, following the highly anticipated Fable, otherwise their IPO in October won't have as much juice. The caveat to this is OpenAI and Anthropic being the single two most disruptive companies to society over the past decade, do you really want to fade their IPO considering their biggest moat is the user behaviour data they've been accumulating on billions of users? Something interesting I've been noticing is people building simulations of games which reflect our current economy and society. Specifically what happens when prices and inflation continues up and what are hard assets/necessities. The realization is that everything is worthless, there's few hard assets and more importantly commodities with controlled supply sinks that can't be inflated due to external inputs. The hardest question over the past several months has been determining what narratives send BTC up. For those who've been around a couple cycles, we all know bottoms form when negative news stops sending prices down. text: JUST IN: MANTRA Chain Halts Network and Freezes All Transactions Amid Unidentified Incident MANTRA Chain, an RWA-focused Layer 1 blockchain, has halted its network as a precaution while investigating an unidentified incident. All endpoints and transactions are currently frozen, temporarily affecting deposits and withdrawals. MANTRA previously raised $11 million and later launched a $108.8 million ecosystem fund, with Nomura's digital asset arm Laser Digital and Brevan Howard Digital among its capital and strategic partners. MANTRA is the project behind the OM token, which plunged approximately 90% within a short period in April 2025. South Korea's largest crypto exchange Upbit has designated MANTRA (OM) as a trading caution asset, affecting the OM/KRW, OM/BTC, and OM/USDT markets. The caution period will run from August 21 to the third week of September (September 14–18). MANTRA Chain said it has identified and contained the root cause of a recent security incident, which was isolated to its Cosmos EVM module and affected two wallet addresses. The team said no user funds were exploited. The network has been halted as a precaution while a patch is being tested. If testing is successful, MANTRA Chain aims to resume operations later today and will publish a full post-mortem afterward. — link

text: UK HMRC Sent More Than 81,000 Crypto Tax Warning Letters in 2025/26 According to Protos, the UK's HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) sent more than 81,000 warning letters to crypto holders suspected of unpaid taxes during the 2025/26 financial year, nearly triple the 27,714 letters sent in 2024. HMRC said the unpaid taxes largely stem from gains made during the crypto bull market between 2022 and 2025. Selling, gifting, swapping or using crypto for purchases may trigger capital gains tax obligations, while unpaid taxes can result in penalties of up to 100% of the amount owed, plus interest.
